- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.5 or lower) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or adjust downward 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is below recent 10-day moving average, model underestimates upward momentum — raise forecast by 2–4% if sentiment > 0.5.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility in 30-day horizon — apply 10–15% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -0.7 → +0.7), model often lags — forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3–5% gap over 5+ days), apply “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–2% from next forecast if sentiment remains flat or mildly negative.
